title: Positioning Buried Electricity Distribution Cables Using RTK-GNSS and Depth Probes: Field Performance in Dense Urban Canyons

record.title: Positioning Buried Electricity Distribution Cables Using RTK-GNSS and Depth Probes: Field Performance in Dense Urban Canyons
record.abstract: Real-time kinematic GNSS is the standard horizontal positioning method for utility cadastre surveys in Serbia, but signal obstruction in narrow urban streets degrades solution quality. This study evaluated horizontal positioning accuracy of RTK-GNSS for utility location work in three street types in Novi Sad: open boulevards, medium-density streets and narrow historic-centre lanes. A Leica GS18 receiver was used with a national reference network connection. Dilution of precision and fix rate were recorded continuously over 140 survey hours. In narrow lanes, fix rate dropped to 63% and horizontal RMS error increased from 1.7 cm to 9.4 cm. A workflow combining short RTK observation windows with constrained total-station traverses bridging signal gaps reduced the lane-canyon horizontal RMS to 3.8 cm. Depth of burial was measured using a direct-read sonde inserted through existing access points. The combined approach achieved 98% of survey points within the 5 cm horizontal accuracy threshold required by Serbian regulation.
